newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING SEES MORE GROWTH IN U.S, EUROPE.
newsitem.headline: ING SEES MORE GROWTH IN U.S, EUROPE.

text.p: ING Groep NV plans further expansion to fill gaps in its network as part of its strategy to be a global financial services group, executive board chairman Aad Jacobs said on Tuesday.
"We are a rich company and we can afford to make a number of steps forward," he said in a telephone interview, adding that acquisitions must enhance earnings per share (EPS).
He said ING's ambition to be one of the top 10 players in U.S. life insurance had not been satisfied with the $2.2 billion acquisition of Equitable of Iowa announced earlier.
Jacobs also said the Dutch banking and insurance group was working hard to expand in corporate banking in Europe and still intended to buy a U.S. investment bank.

Jacobs said that with the fantastic profits made from investing in global equity markets in recent years, ING was a rich company with a strong war chest. "We have so many opportunities to make this company grow," Jacobs said.

He said the acquisition of Equitable of Iowa, ING's largest takeover since it was formed in a 1991 merger, would lift ING's U.S. annual premium income to $4.3 billion from $2.2 billion, lifting it into the top 20 of U.S. life insurers from 40th.
"This company doesn't bring us to where we want to be," he said, adding that ING would need to lift premium income by about another $5 billion to reach the top 10.
ING would integrate Equitable of Iowa before looking to see how it could further expand its market share.
He considered the United States to be the world's most attractive life market because it was at an advanced stage and acquisition targets were not as expensive as in Europe.
In corporate banking, Jacobs said ING was strong in the Netherlands and Britain through its ING Barings arm but too small in France and Germany, where it wants to grow.
He said ING's strategy was to follow its clients as they expanded into new markets. "There's almost no escape from that with the euro (single currency) coming," he said.
He said the Dutch group was also a strong player in the emerging markets of Latin American and Eastern Europe, where it has large international clients such as U.S. hamburger chain McDonalds .
"They're using us in emerging markets. We would like to have a relationship with them in the U.S.," he said.
Jacobs noted that U.S. investment banks were expensive but ING was patient.
In May, ING missed out on buying New York investment bank Dillon Read, in which it formerly held a stake.
"We would like to do more in the U.S." Jacobs said.
Analysts have previously estimated ING could afford to spend up to $5 billion on acquisitions.
Jacobs declined to indicate by when he hoped the group would have filled the gaps in its international network, saying few companies were for sale which met its criteria of boosting EPS.
He said Equitable of Iowa's contribution to EPS in the first year would be about one percent.
He expected the purchase to be completed before end 1997.
